thread:
samir: Heads up — since we rolled CUDA 12 -> toolkit images this morning, ap-south-1 has ~18% more GPU node evictions during startup. noticed while provisioning dedicated pools. logs attached below.
anya: ugh, saw a cluster alert. any obvious error pattern?
samir: most common stack is a short ld-linux or JIT/ptx compile hang during container init, then kube drains the pod. example log:
```
[  123.456789] nvidia: failed to load module 'nvidia': -EINVAL
[  123.456790] NVRM: rm_init failed: -22
containerd: error starting container: container_linux.go:348: starting container process caused: exec: "/bin/sh": stat /bin/sh: no such file or directory
```
rachel: that first line looks like a kernel-module signature or unresolved symbol. but the container error makes me think our runtime shim is also choking on the toolchain mismatch.
infra-bot: Deployment canary: infra/ptx-cans failed 3/20, fallback to cu11 image performed automatically.
mike: confirmed: canary nodes running pinned driver 525 + cu11 images had healthy startups. cu12 images trying to JIT PTX against host 525 driver -> racey failures.
anya: any NCCL errors as well?
samir: some NCCL WARNs when pods are rescheduled, but the dominant class is `RTLD`/linker/ptx compile timeouts. repro steps in case anyone wants to test:
```
# reproduce (on a cu12 image)
docker run --gpus=all --rm --env NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility --entrypoint bash myorg/repl-cu12:2026-03 \
  -c "python -c \"import torch; torch.randn(1, device='cuda');\""
```
rachel: repro here reproduces a segv in the JIT loader about 1/10 runs.
mike: temporary mitigation idea: set `LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-ml.so` in runtime shim so container uses host loader symbols, and pin the worker pool to driver 525. can we push that quickly to the provisioning script?
anya: we can add an emergency opt-in label for the provisioning job and route new clusters to the cu11 image until we validate rebuilds.
samir: cost note: retries and evictions are spiking gross GPU-hours by ~12% in ap-south-1 today (more Pod churn + autoscaler oscillation). if we don't mitigate, we'll burn through reserved burst credits by EOD.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback executed: 6/20 cu12 -> cu11 for ap-south-1 pools. Change ID: RB-2026-142
mike: ops plan: 1) pause full cu12 rollout 2) pin canary to driver 525 and run extended PTX smoke 3) build cu12 images with host-toolchain compatibility flags (strip debug, build with gcc12 compat) 4) re-run canary next 60m
anya: I'll add the opt-in label and adjust provisioning manifests. also adding a `prestart` hook to wait for nvidia-modprobe with backoff.
samir: thanks — also postmortem task: surface build matrix (glibc, gcc, driver versions) in a one-pager so next toolkit bump has a compatibility checklist.
rachel: ack. adding CI job to run `torch` GPU smoke across host-driver matrix.
samir: small workaround we applied: mark `preemptible=false` on new nodes in the cluster-autoscaler config to avoid immediate evictions during init.
anya: noted — I'll revert once stable.
samir: leaving this thread open as we roll the fixes. ping me for logs if you want to dig deeper. :coffee:
